landing.lede: Entry, stop, target, close — each one goes out to every connected account at the same moment, sized to that account's own balance. When one exchange fails, the rest still fill and you get told which one didn't.

margin.label: Of balance
margin.body: committed as margin on every entry

connect.body: Each account is verified on connect and refused outright if the key can withdraw. Keys are encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser.

trade.body: One ticket sets side, leverage and the stop and target percentages. The engine sizes each account from its own balance and dispatches every leg concurrently.

watch.body: Per-leg results arrive as they happen. A failed leg raises a notice that stays on screen until you dismiss it — no toast that disappears while you look away.

features.title: Six constraints, not six buttons
features.body: Every trade obeys these. They are guarantees someone is trusting with their capital, so they earn their space.

isolation.body: Every account gets its own connection, its own rate limit and its own deadline. An exchange going down costs that account the trade and nobody else.

sizing.body: Every account commits 99% of its own USDT. A $50 account and a $5,000 account take the same leverage and the same stop percentage, at very different dollar sizes.

stops.body: Drag the stop on the chart, edit it in the ticket, or change it on the position row — all three push the same amendment to every account.

keys.body: Trade-only is enforced at connect wherever the exchange exposes the permission; a key that can move money is refused outright.

mark.term: The exchange is the source of truth
mark.body: Positions are re-read from each venue on a timer, so a stop that fired on the exchange closes the leg here — and a position the platform wrote off is put back.

statements.body: Every account gets its own page and a PDF statement in the language its partner reads — money only, no percentages that invite misreading.

live.title: The fan-out, live
live.body: Signed in, this is your own last trade, leg by leg. Signed out, the diagram runs the demo so the promise still teaches itself.

security.title: It holds live trading credentials
security.body: Keys are encrypted at rest with rotatable Fernet keys, never logged, never included in an API response, and verified as non-withdrawable at connect time wherever the exchange exposes a permission endpoint. Where it cannot be proven, the account is flagged rather than silently trusted.
security.item1: Keys encrypted at rest with rotatable Fernet keys — never logged, never in an API response.
security.item2: Trade-only enforced at connect: a key that can withdraw is refused outright wherever the exchange lets us check.
security.item3: Credentials are never sent back to the browser, not even masked for display.
security.item4: Where an exchange publishes no permission endpoint, the account is flagged rather than silently trusted.
security.item5: A platform-wide halt switch (STOP_ALL) that stops new routing instantly and cannot be cleared from the panel.

faq.title: Questions an operator asks
faq.body: Straight answers, including the ones it costs nothing to be honest about.
faq.q1: Has this been tested against live exchanges?
faq.a1: Not yet. The eight adapters are written from vendored exchange documentation and unit-tested against mocked transports, but none has been run against a live exchange or testnet. Verify on testnet before committing real capital.
faq.a2: Hyperliquid, Bybit, Binance, OKX, Gate.io, KuCoin, Toobit and LBank sit behind one interface. Capability differences — native versus emulated stops, per-symbol versus per-account leverage — are handled behind the adapter seam, never in trading logic.
faq.q3: Can the keys move money out?
faq.a3: No. Every key is verified as trade-only at connect, and refused outright where withdrawal rights are detected. On exchanges that publish no permission endpoint, the check is reported as unprovable and the account is flagged rather than quietly trusted.
faq.a4: Sizing is 99% of an account's available USDT balance, with leverage on top. An account denominated in anything else is reported on the dashboard as unusable — it is never traded on a guess.
faq.a5: One open trade per account. An entry whose fill is unconfirmed counts as possibly holding one, so a second order can never stack on a position that may already be there.
faq.q6: What if one exchange fails mid-trade?
faq.a6: That account fails alone and raises a persistent notice that stays until you dismiss it — the others still fill. A leg that failed after its order went out is re-read from the exchange, so a fill is never reported as a failure.

bots.title: Bots
bots.lead: A bot is a signal source, not a second execution path. A Pine Script strategy decides the side; sizing, the fan-out and the halt are the same code the manual button goes through. Only one bot runs at a time — starting another stops whichever one was running.
bots.strategiesLead: Pine Script v5, checked as you type. Anything outside the supported subset is refused by name, line and column — nothing is parsed and quietly ignored.
bots.backtestLead: Replay a version over stored history. The fill model is printed above the metrics, because a backtest that flatters itself produces a number people act on.
bots.noneBody: A bot runs one version of one strategy on one pair. Write the strategy first.
bots.noStrategiesBody: A strategy is a Pine Script v5 file. Saving a version never rewrites an old one, so a running bot cannot change under it.
bots.sizingNote: Size is not a setting: every account is sized at 99% of its own balance. A qty in the script is ignored and reported at upload.
bots.gateBlocks: The promotion gate is not met yet
bots.gateUnmet: {name} has not met the promotion gate

bots.noAutoResume: Nothing here resumes on its own. A bot that stopped itself is restarted by a person who has read why.
bots.noActionsBody: Every order this bot sends appears here with the result each account gave back.
bots.promotionHint: Measured, not asserted. Live is refused while any row is unmet.
bots.gateFootnote: One row cannot be measured from inside: no exchange adapter has been run against a live exchange or a testnet yet. It is carried as an explicit acknowledgement rather than quietly assumed.
bots.sourceHint: The exact version this bot runs. Read-only: a version is immutable, so a running bot cannot change under it.

security.title: Security
security.hint: Every control here is off until you turn it on, and none of them touch order routing.
security.pinnedOffBody: SECURITY_FEATURES=false in the environment holds the whole layer off. Nothing on this card can be armed until that is changed on the server — which is deliberate: it is the escape hatch if a control ever locks you out.

two_factor.label: Ask for a code at sign-in
two_factor.hint: A six-digit code from an authenticator app, on top of the password. Recovery codes are issued during enrolment and each one works once.
two_factor.blocked: Enrol an authenticator app and save the recovery codes first.

trusted_devices.label: Remember this browser
trusted_devices.hint: Lets a browser you have already verified skip the code. Without this, a code every single time is a control that gets switched off within a week.
trusted_devices.blocked: Turn on the code at sign-in first.

login_rate_limit.label: Slow down repeated wrong passwords
login_rate_limit.hint: After a run of failures the same address has to wait. Applies to the sign-in form and to the password prompt below — never to routing an order.

new_device_notice.label: Notify me about a sign-in from a new browser
new_device_notice.hint: Raises a notification that stays until you dismiss it, like a failed order does. On one shared login this is the only sign that somebody else got in.

idle_timeout.label: Sign out an idle browser
idle_timeout.hint: The session expires after a period of no activity, and again at a hard age however active it is.

single_session.label: One browser at a time
single_session.hint: Signing in ends every other session on this login. Useful when the password has been shared and you want it back.

ip_allowlist.label: Only allow these addresses
ip_allowlist.hint: Everything except the emergency halt and the health check is refused from an address that is not on the list.

step_up.label: Ask for the password again before sensitive changes
step_up.hint: Covers connecting or removing an account, editing the money records, changing these switches, and putting a bot live. Never a trade.

audit_log.label: Keep an access history
audit_log.hint: Records sign-ins, refusals, and changes to these switches. A change to the switches themselves is always recorded, even with this off.

admin_write_rate_limit.label: Cap how fast settings can be changed
admin_write_rate_limit.hint: Applies to the admin endpoints only. Orders, balances, the halt and the bot endpoints are excluded by name.

csp_mode.label: Content-Security-Policy
csp_mode.hint: Tells the browser which scripts and connections the panel is allowed to make. Start on report-only, watch the console for a day, then enforce.

fields.idleCost: This is the one control that adds a write to every request — the session's deadline moves forward. It costs one small update, and nothing else on this card costs anything while it is off.
fields.stepUpScope: Opening, amending and closing a position are never guarded, and neither is the emergency halt. A password prompt in front of those costs money during the minute it matters most.
fields.writeLimitScope: Order routing, balances, the halt and the bot endpoints are excluded whatever this says.
fields.allowed_ipsHint: One per line. A single address or a CIDR block, e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 203.0.113.0/24.
fields.allowlistEscape: Your current address is added automatically when you turn this on, so saving cannot lock you out. The emergency halt stays reachable from anywhere regardless.

totp.title: Set up an authenticator app
totp.removeBody: This deletes the enrolled device, forgets every remembered browser, and switches the code prompt off — leaving it on with nothing enrolled would ask for a code nobody can produce.
totp.scanBody: Scan this with Google Authenticator, 1Password, Aegis or any TOTP app.
totp.manualKey: Or enter this key by hand
totp.manualHint: Only needed if the app cannot scan. Treat it like a password.
totp.confirmBody: Enter the current six-digit code to prove the app has the key.
totp.saveWarning: These are shown once and cannot be shown again. Each works a single time. Save them somewhere you can reach without this panel — they are how you get back in if the phone is lost.

stepUp.title: Confirm your password
stepUp.body: This change is one of the few that asks again. Your confirmation covers the next few minutes in this browser.

events.hint: Sign-ins, refusals, and changes to the switches above.
events.emptyBody: Sign-ins and refusals will appear here as they happen.
events.offBody: Turn on “Keep an access history” above to start recording sign-ins and refusals. Changes to the switches are recorded either way.
